title: The Risky Project Worth $52,000, Not $35,000
featured_title: THE RISKY PROJECT WORTH 52000 DOLLARS NOT 35000
subject: other-disciplines

presentation.challenge: The outcomes were not equally likely. Probability-weighting gives an expected value of $52,000, not the simple average of $35,000.

practice.primary_question: How is expected monetary value calculated when project outcomes have different probabilities?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Using a simple average of unequal-probability outcomes.

case_dna.target_misconception: A risky project's outcomes can be averaged equally regardless of their probabilities.
case_dna.why_plausible: The arithmetic mean is familiar and easy to apply.
case_dna.corrected_model: Expected monetary value is the probability-weighted sum of mutually exclusive outcomes.

problem_statement: Project R has a 60% probability of +$120,000 and a 40% probability of -$50,000. A guaranteed alternative returns +$45,000. Determine Project R's EMV and the preferred alternative under an expected-value criterion.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: Unequal probabilities were treated as equal weights.

options.label: Use the arithmetic mean of payoffs
options.reason: The outcomes are not equally likely.

options.label: Use only the favorable payoff
options.reason: All stated outcomes must be included.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the expected value
gates.hint: The loss outcome contributes a negative weighted payoff.

cards.text: EMV=$52,000, which is $7,000 above the guaranteed alternative.

correction.template: Project R EMV=${emv}, which is ${advantage} above the guaranteed alternative.

options.label: Choose the guaranteed alternative because it has no loss state
options.reason: That may reflect risk preference, but not the stated expected-value criterion.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply expected value again
gates.prompt: A project has 30% chance of +$200,000 and 70% chance of -$40,000. What is EMV?

options.reason: That is the simple average of payoffs.

gates.explanation: Expected value includes each payoff weighted by its probability.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the decision analysis
gates.confirmation: I confirm that expected monetary value is a probability-weighted sum.

items.label: What was missed
items.value: The favorable and loss states have different probabilities.

seo.seo_title: Expected Monetary Value Project Selection | FE E-096
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Other Disciplines E-096: 60% at +$120,000 and 40% at -$50,000 gives EMV=$52,000.
seo.focus_keyphrase: FE expected monetary value project selection
seo.excerpt: Risky project outcomes must be weighted by their probabilities before comparison.
seo.direct_answer: EMV=0.60($120,000)+0.40(-$50,000)=$52,000. Under the stated expected-value criterion, this exceeds the guaranteed $45,000 alternative by $7,000.

faqs.a: The probability-weighted sum of all possible monetary outcomes.

faqs.q: Can risk preference produce a different choice?
faqs.a: Yes. This case uses expected value as the stated criterion.
